name: NTT Silicon Valley SV1 Data Center

source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.reading:
Per NTT's own Global Data Centers facility page, this building, NTT Silicon Valley SV1, is located at 1160 Walsh Ave., Santa Clara, CA 95050. The operator publishes 64,000 square feet of data floor (technical) space and 16 megawatts of critical IT load for this specific building; the page does not list a separate total building square footage or a year the facility opened, and no formal certifications (SOC, ISO, PCI, Uptime Tier) are named on this specific page. NTT DATA Group, the parent of NTT's Global Data Centers business, is a Japanese public company listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange and is not an SEC 10-K filer.

California regulators are actively reworking how large data center loads are billed and interconnected as demand grows statewide. Under SB 57 (2025), the California Public Utilities Commission opened a rate-design rulemaking in April 2026 specifically addressing electric rate impacts of data centers and other large transmission-connected loads, an inquiry expected to run roughly two years and examine dedicated data-center tariffs and the risk of costs shifting onto residential and small-business ratepayers. The California Independent System Operator separately published a formal issue paper on large-load interconnection considerations in January 2026, part of an ongoing CAISO regulatory track addressing how data centers and other large loads connect to the state's transmission grid. Santa Clara's municipal utility, Silicon Valley Power, and the broader South Bay grid have absorbed years of hyperscale and colocation growth predating this rulemaking, making Silicon Valley one of the most power-constrained data center submarkets the state regulators are now studying.

NTT's US Global Data Centers footprint spans seven named campuses in total: Ashburn, Virginia at 224 megawatts; Chicago, Illinois at more than 200 megawatts; Dallas, Texas at 160 megawatts; Hillsboro, Oregon at 126 megawatts; Phoenix, Arizona at 240 megawatts; and a combined Sacramento/Santa Clara, California figure of 68 megawatts, totaling roughly 1,118 megawatts or more of disclosed US capacity, per the operator's own locations page. The US business operates under the NTT DATA Global Data Centers Americas name, the successor brand to RagingWire Data Centers, now under Japan's NTT DATA Group and parent Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corporation, a Tokyo Stock Exchange-listed company not subject to SEC 10-K filing requirements.

reading.body:
NTT Silicon Valley SV1 publishes 16 MW of IT capacity at 1160 Walsh Ave., Santa Clara. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 16 MW is roughly 400 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a more typical colocation average, it is closer to 1,600 racks. The arithmetic shifts sharply with rack density, and NTT does not publish a per-rack power figure for this site, so neither number should be read as the operator's claim.

No certifications are listed in the published specifications for this facility, so no statement can be made about what compliance tiers it has achieved. Tenant names, pricing, and available capacity are not published on the operator page this site read.

Among the 103 facilities mapped in California, only five publish a megawatt figure at all. SV1's 16 MW ranks third among those five, which together total 170 MW of published IT capacity, meaning this single campus accounts for roughly 9 percent of what this site can actually count in the state. That share reflects the scarcity of published data more than it reflects the true size of California's data center market, but it does establish SV1 as a meaningful, mid-tier presence within the subset of California facilities that are legible by published numbers.
